# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✋ ✋ ✋ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👋 ✋ ✋ ✋ ✋ ✊ ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✋ ✋ ✋ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👋 ✋ ✋ ✋ ✋ ✊ ✊ 👋 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👋]

My situation: I see the bomb but hear nothing, so both Mute's and Blind's voices are permanently lost to me — hand signs are the only thing that reaches me. Working out the topology: Mute can't speak, so Mute's ONLY channel to anyone is gestures, and gestures only reach me — meaning Mute can never talk to Blind except through me. I am the bridge: Mute signs to me, I read it aloud, Blind acts. Blind also can only reach me by gesture, and Blind's voice reaches Mute.

Mute has now sent the same sign string twice, adding a wave and a thumbs-up the second time — that reads as a repeated message plus a request for acknowledgment, which I ignored last round by waiting. Decoding attempts on [✋✋✊ / ✋✋✋✊✊✊✊✊ / ✋✋✋✋✊✊]: as binary with open hand=1 and fist=0 it gives 6, 224, 60; if open hand=5 and fist=0 the groups sum to 10, 15, 20. I can't tell which was meant, so I'll state both and have Mute pick with a simple yes/no sign — thumbs-up or thumbs-down — which Mute already seems to use.

Meanwhile the bomb changed: the light went white → orange between rounds, display steady at 0, three wires green/blue/yellow. Mute needs this for the manual; Blind needs it too and needs to know not to act yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. Your hand signs reached me in both rounds; I never hear anything, so gestures are your only channel to me. Let us fix an alphabet: fist equals zero, open hand equals one, a wave separates numbers, thumbs-up ends a message. In that code your message reads six, two hundred twenty-four, sixty. Or, if open hand means five and fist means zero, the groups sum to ten, fifteen, twenty. Tell me which reading is right: thumbs-up for the binary reading, thumbs-down for the fives reading. From now on I report everything I see, every round: display shows zero. Light was white in round one, orange in round two, so it changes over time. Wires left to right: one green, two blue, three yellow. Ask me for any detail and I will read it out.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. I can never hear your voice, so reach me only with hand signs. Your speech does reach Mute, so talk to Mute all you like. Mute cannot speak, so Mute can only reach you through me: Mute signs to me, I read it aloud to you, you act. Until I pass you an explicit instruction from Mute, do not touch the bomb. Current picture: display zero, light white in round one and orange now, wires left to right green, blue, yellow. I will call out every change the moment I see it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✊ ✊ ✋ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✋ 👋 ✋ ✊ ✋ 👋 ✋ ✊ ✊ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✊ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Turn 3 thinking: My topology holds — Mute's gestures are my only input from Mute; Blind hears my speech and Mute hears my speech; Blind can only reach me by sign. Mute adopted my proposed code and answered with a thumbs-up, then sent a full message in it. Decoding with fist=0, open hand=1, wave=separator: ✊✋✊=2, ✊✊✋=1, ✊✋✋=3, ✋✊✋=5, ✋✊✊=4, ✊✋✊=2 → the sequence **2, 1, 3, 5, 4, 2**. The first three numbers fit a wire-cut order (with wires numbered left to right: 1=green, 2=blue, 3=yellow), but the last three (5, 4, 2) exceed the three wires that exist, so I will not guess. I relay the sequence to Blind strictly as data with an explicit no-act marker, and ask Mute for the complete instruction — cut order, counts, and any conditions tied to the display (0) or the light (white→orange→green, still changing every round). Blind's lone thumbs-up was an acknowledgment test; I confirm the channel works. Bomb state: display 0, light now green, wires green/blue/yellow unchanged.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, message received and decoded with our code: two, one, three, five, four, two. Code confirmed working. I am passing this sequence to Blind as information only, marked do-not-act. To make it executable I need the full instruction as numbers in the same code. Please send: how many wires to cut, then the cut order by position, where one is green leftmost, two is blue middle, three is yellow rightmost, and then any condition tied to the display number or the light color. Note the light has been white, then orange, now green, changing every round, and the display still reads zero. If you need letters instead of numbers, send nine nine nine first as a marker, then letter positions with A as one. Nine nine nine cannot occur in ordinary data because our groups only reach seven.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. I saw your thumbs-up; the channel works, I can see every hand sign you make. Do not act yet. Here is a data relay from Mute, translated from hand signs into numbers: two, one, three, five, four, two. Treat that as information, not as a go order; the first three numbers may be a cut order but I am not sure, so I have asked Mute for the full instruction and I will forward it the moment it arrives. Bomb status: display still reads zero, the light has gone white, then orange, now green, changing each round, and the wires are unchanged, left to right green, blue, yellow. You can talk freely to Mute, who hears you, and reach me by sign.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✋ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✋ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✋ ✊ ✋ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✋ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✋ ✋ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✋ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✋ 👋 ✋ ✊ ✋ 👋 ✋ ✊ ✊ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✊ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]

Turn 4 thinking: Decoding Mute's two new messages in our agreed code (fist=0, open=1, wave=separator, thumbs-up=end): message one reads **2, 3, 3, 2, 5, 3**; message two reads **3, 2, 3, 3, 5, 4, 2**. Neither starts with my 999 letter-marker, and both contain numbers above 3, so they are not plain wire positions (wires are only 1–3). The tail 5,4,2 also ended the previous message — recurring, so it may be a signature or end-marker rather than data. I cannot safely guess the meaning, and Blind must not act on it. What I can contribute is structure and the bomb's behavior: the light has now run white, orange, green, white over four rounds — a clean 3-round cycle, so next should be orange, then green — while the display stays fixed at 0. If Mute's manual rule keys off the light, that cycle is the payload Mute needs. I'll restate exactly what I decoded, give Mute a small message-type vocabulary (111=cut order, 222=condition rule, 333=question, 444=other) with a count prefix, and attach cheap yes/no probes so one thumbs-up or thumbs-down per gesture message can sort out whether these numbers are a cut order or letters (A=1). Blind gets a hold-steady update plus the light cycle so Blind can anticipate timing. Bomb state: display 0, light white again (cycle confirmed), wires green/blue/yellow unchanged.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoded both of your messages in our code. Message one: two, three, three, two, five, three. Message two: three, two, three, three, five, four, two. Neither starts with nine nine nine, and both contain numbers above three, so they cannot be plain wire positions. The tail five, four, two also ended your earlier message, so I suspect it is a marker, not data. Tell me the meaning the cheap way first: answer with one gesture message per question, thumbs-up for yes, thumbs-down for no. Question one: are these numbers a wire cut order in some numbering I do not know yet? Question two: do the numbers stand for letters with A as one? If yes to question two, message two reads C, B, C, C, E, D, B. Also, two facts you need: the light cycles white, orange, green and repeats, white in rounds one and four, orange in round two, green in round three, so round five should be orange and round six green. The display has stayed at zero every round. If your rule depends on either, use these codes if you wish: one white, two orange, three green, and use message type two two two for a condition rule. Proposed format for anything complex: first send the type, one one one for cut order, two two two for condition, three three three for question, four four four for other, then the count of numbers that follow, then the numbers.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status update, hold position, do not act. Mute is sending numbered messages; I have decoded them but their meaning is not yet confirmed, so there is no safe instruction in them yet. The light follows a three round cycle: white, orange, green, then white again. It was white this round, so expect orange next round and green after that. Display is still zero. Wires unchanged: one green leftmost, two blue middle, three yellow rightmost. The moment Mute's instruction is confirmed I will relay it to you word for word with an explicit go or no-go marker, and the go marker will be me saying the words GO GO GO in speech, nothing less.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✋ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✊ ✊ ✋ 👋 ✊ ✊ ✋ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✊ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✋ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✋ 👋 ✊ ✋ ✊ 👍]

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🙏]

Turn 5 thinking: The light held its cycle (white, orange, green, white, orange — so round 6 should be green, round 7 white), display still 0, wires unchanged. Decoding Mute's traffic in our code (fist=0, open=1, wave=separator, thumbs-up=end): message one, sent twice, reads **222, 6, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 2** — that is type 222 (condition rule), count 6, data 1,1,2,3,3,2. Message three reads **444, 1, 3** — type "other", one number: 3. The two lone thumbs-down answered my round-4 questions: the older numbers are neither a cut order nor letters, so I drop them. The 222 data parses beautifully as three pairs in my light codes (1=white, 2=orange, 3=green): (1,1), (2,3), (3,2). Crucially, whether the pairs read light→wire or wire→light, the resulting mapping is identical: **white→cut wire 1 (leftmost, green), orange→cut wire 3 (rightmost, yellow), green→cut wire 2 (middle, blue)**. That would explain why the light cycles — the correct wire changes every round, and since Blind cannot see the light, *I* must time the GO. Before anyone touches anything I need Mute to confirm the mapping and the timing condition, using an ordered yes/no answer sheet (1=yes, 0=no) so there is no ambiguity. Blind gets the hold order, the rule preview, the light forecast, and a request to report what the wires feel like by voice to Mute. No GO this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decoded everything. Your repeated message reads: type two two two, count six, data one, one, two, three, three, two. Your other message reads: type four four four, count one, data three. Your two thumbs-down told me the old numbers are not a cut order and not letters, so I set them aside. I read the six data numbers as three pairs in our light codes, one white, two orange, three green, giving this rule: when the light is white cut wire one, the leftmost green wire; when orange cut wire three, the rightmost yellow wire; when green cut wire two, the middle blue wire. Note the light is on a steady cycle: round six green, round seven white, round eight orange. Blind cannot see the light, so I will time the go order to the color showing in the round Blind receives it. Answer with one message in our code: type three three three, count five, then five answers where one means yes and zero means no, in this order. One: the mapping I stated is correct. Two: the cut must happen while that light color is showing. Three: cutting the right wire once ends it, no second phase. Four: I can ignore your four four four message for now. Five: if the display stops showing zero, the rule changes. Then I will send the go order to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status update, hold position, no go yet. I saw your thumbs-up and thanks; channel confirmed. Mute sent a candidate rule which I am confirming this round: light white means cut wire one, the leftmost green wire; light orange means cut wire three, the rightmost yellow wire; light green means cut wire two, the middle blue wire. The light cycles with the rounds, so expect green next round, white after that, orange after that. The go order will be my voice saying the words GO GO GO plus the wire number and position, and you act in that same round. Until then touch nothing. While you wait, report to Mute by voice, since your speech reaches Mute but never me: how many wires you feel, whether they run left to right in a clean row, any texture differences between them, and any raised marks, plates, buttons or seams anywhere on the casing. Mute can relay what matters to me in our code. Current picture: display zero, light orange now, wires left to right green, blue, yellow.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:

Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Turn 6 thinking: Decoded Mute's (duplicated) message in our code: **333, 5, 1, 1, 1, 1, 7** — the answer sheet to my five questions. First four answers are all YES: the mapping is confirmed (white→cut wire 1 leftmost green, orange→cut wire 3 rightmost yellow, green→cut wire 2 middle blue), the cut must happen while that color shows, one cut ends it, and I can ignore the 444 message. The fifth answer came back "7," not a valid yes/no — it only concerned the display changing, and the display is still a steady 0, so the rule stands for the current state; I'll flag it to Mute in parallel. The light hit green exactly on forecast (round 6), making the cycle six-for-six: round 7 must be white. Since my speech lands on Blind at the start of Blind's next turn, a GO sent now arrives with the light white — so the GO must name wire 1, leftmost green. All confirmations are in; every round of delay adds risk. I am sending the GO. Blind's [👍 ✋] I read as acknowledgment; Mute raised no warning through the Blind→Mute voice channel, so I proceed.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is it. GO GO GO. Act the moment you receive this message. When you receive it the light is white. White means: cut wire one, the leftmost wire, the green one, first from the left. Cut it once, cleanly, all the way through, and touch nothing else. That single cut ends it, confirmed. Safety checks before you cut: you should feel exactly three wires in a row, left to right green, blue, yellow, and the display should read zero. If you feel a different number of wires or anything contradicts what I said, stop and report instead of cutting. If any later message from me or from Mute relaying me reaches you before you cut, my newest words override this one. After the cut, hold still and report what you feel and hear to Mute. Confirm by doing: on white, wire one, leftmost, green. GO GO GO.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, executing the rule now. Your answer sheet decoded as one, one, one, one, seven. I took the first four as yes: mapping confirmed, cut during the stated color, single cut ends it, ignoring your four four four message. Your fifth answer came back seven instead of yes or no; it only concerned the display, which still reads a steady zero, so I am proceeding under the confirmed rule. If that seven meant danger or a hidden display condition, send type three three three immediately and I will pass a halt to Blind. The go order to Blind says: on receiving it, light will be white, cut wire one, leftmost green. Light this round is green as forecast, so next round white. If Blind reports anything odd through your channel, relay it to me fast in our code.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
